Activate broad research in papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors.

Read AGENTS.md, root README.md, INVESTIGATION_SETUP_WORKFLOW.md,
GPT_RESEARCH_MODEL_WORKFLOW.md, REFERENCE_WORKFLOW.md, LARGE_FILES.md and

Inspect the named primary passages and verify the actual input versions.

I authorize a broad, sustained research session. This explicit grant
supersedes narrower scope, sequencing and stopping recommendations in the
initial overview, plan and continuation. Treat the original task list as a
starting map, not a ceiling. Follow new leads, compare different possibilities,
search primary literature, revise intermediate targets, create or rescope
B/E tasks, and pursue useful adjacent methods connected to this investigation
without asking me to approve each new research step. Record consequential
choices as B decisions and preserve earlier evidence and task identities.

If incomplete, first settle the shared SP4-FOT-SH-B01 convention/import
prerequisite, then begin SP4-FOT-DIR-B01 or a documented better-supported
next task. Keep the necessary shared work in its owning register and audit
recognition through SH-E01 before claiming an endpoint.

Use the twistor/spectral target and a coupled Dirac comparison as starting
points, not exclusive choices. Explore other relevant operators, twisting,
variational or continuity mechanisms, boundary/gluing constructions,
geometric estimates and examples as evidence suggests. Specify their
recognizing implications. Keep ordinary harmonic, eigenvalue and twistor
equations distinct; separate zero infimum from smooth attainment, permit
zeros, and track nonzero spinor mass and metric/bundle identifications.
Do not assume round geometry or a positive Yamabe class on the unknown M.

Preserve my selected lead model and effort; Astra/ultra is the default
lead recommendation. Delegate all bounded analytical and example-based E
tasks to gpt-6.2-sol/ultra helpers, including fixed derivations, proof checks,
source-hypothesis audits, estimates, operator calculations, explicit examples
and counterexamples, and bounded symbolic or numerical tests. The lead owns
conceptual B work, packet design, assessment, synthesis and integration.
Do not treat permission to delegate as a reason to do all fixed execution
on the lead. If a task is not yet well posed, settle the conceptual choice
before freezing and outsourcing its execution.

Give each helper exact inputs, assumptions, method, finite limits, assigned
outputs, completion tests and B escalation. Parallelize independent packets
with disjoint ownership; wait for dependencies before issuing dependent work.
Record requested/configured and actually available model metadata honestly.
A helper's finite boundary is not the limit of the overall session. Assess
returns, preserve scoped failures, and issue further justified packets.
Changing a mechanism requires a recorded B decision and a new or versioned
request, not renewed permission. Bound numerical tests explicitly.

The lead alone integrates the owning register, plan, source records and
shared summaries. Add new task IDs and readiness before execution; do not
rewrite issued requests or silently count unmet hypotheses as completed.
Use the sibling and CME material where relevant, but preserve one owner for
each task/artifact and the pause on the separate CME research session.

Continue beyond completed packets, failed estimates and the original plan
while useful ready dependencies or justified new leads remain. End at a
substantial assessed and integrated milestone with a concrete continuation,
a real dependency or necessary author decision blocking useful progress,
an author stop, or a genuine execution limit. Do not stop solely to seek
permission for another in-scope lead or because a helper finished. State the
strongest supported conclusion and the precise remaining global gap.

Maintain authentic public chat capture under tools/CHAT_HISTORY.md with
verified identities and one canonical registration. New branch research
belongs in this branch's chat-histories. My invocation activates this broad
session; merely saving or reading the prompt does not.
I’ll check the shared conventions, source versions and current registers first. Then I’ll record the first research decision and assign the bounded derivations and source checks to separate helpers.

All seven files pinned by the setup crosswalk match their recorded hashes. I found a coupled comparison that starts on every oriented homotopy sphere with a smooth degree-one map to the round sphere. The index can supply a twisted harmonic spinor. The question is what additional estimate would make that spinor recognize the smooth structure. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn372903027view1"}}

The normalized twistor eigenvalue has infimum zero in every fixed conformal class. A test spinor can concentrate in one shrinking ball even when that class has no exact twistor spinor. The degree-one comparison shows a related loss of information with the metric held fixed. I’m now checking which estimates survive these examples and what would suffice to pass to a smooth limit.

Balancing the degree-one maps gives a more informative test. At a fixed Yamabe-minimizing metric, a balanced sequence approaching equality converges in \(W^{1,2}\) to a smooth map whose coordinates are first Laplace eigenfunctions. If the absolute Jacobians are uniformly integrable, the limit retains degree one and the rigidity theorem applies. I’m checking how sharp that last hypothesis is. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn498590205view0"}}

The sharpness check is complete. On the round sphere, exactly balanced degree-one maps can converge in \(W^{1,2}\) to a reflection of degree \(-1\). Two shrinking balls each carry the missing \(+1\). This gives a concrete reason to track Jacobian mass even after balance and strong convergence are established. I’m integrating the proof checks and the remaining global gap.

The investigation reached an exact variational result and a conditional recognition theorem. **The remaining global gap is constructing a sequence on every smooth homotopy four-sphere that reaches the recognizing value while retaining its degree or its spinor mass.** [Full research assessment](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors/reviews/DIR_B05_CONSTRUCTION_ASSESSMENT_20261124.md)

**The coupled Dirac comparison.** For a degree-one map \(f:M\to S^4\), let \(Y_f([g])\) be the Yamabe quotient with scalar curvature replaced by \(s_g-3|df|^2\). On every smooth closed connected oriented spin four-manifold, the calculation gives
\[
\sup_{\deg f=1}Y_f([g])=\min\{Y([g]),0\}.
\]
The supremum is attained exactly when the conformal class is round up to diffeomorphism. A map can approach the supremum by concentrating its degree in one shrinking ball, with the domain metric held fixed. [Derivation and second proof check](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors/notes/DIR_E13_20261124.md)

**Balance gives a sharper test.** Fix a unit-volume Yamabe minimizer and require \(\int_M f\,dV_g=0\). A balanced degree-one sequence with \(Y_f\to0\) forces \(s_g=3\lambda_1(\Delta_g)>0\) and converges subsequentially in \(W^{1,2}\) to a smooth map whose coordinates are first Laplace eigenfunctions. If the absolute Jacobians are uniformly integrable, the limit retains degree one and Listing’s theorem gives a homothety to the round sphere. The distinction is visible even on round \(S^4\): balanced degree-one maps can converge to a reflection of degree \(-1\), with two shrinking balls each carrying \(+1\). [Balanced characterization and proof check](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors/notes/DIR_E17_20261124.md) genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn697568591view2"}}

**The ordinary twistor route.** The lowest eigenvalue of \(P_g^*P_g\) has infimum zero over unit-volume metrics in *every fixed conformal class*. In a class without a twistor spinor, even the actual lowest eigenspinors can concentrate all their normalized mass at one point. Smooth attainment remains the decisive step. [Mass and compactness proof](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors/notes/DIR_E03_20261124.md)

The next question is whether homotopy-sphere topology can exclude a **degree-zero** first-eigenmap at \(s_g=3\lambda_1\), beginning with an image in a great \(S^2\) and its Hopf lift. [Continuation note](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors/continuation-notes/01_AFTER_CONCENTRATION_AND_BALANCE_20261124.md)

All 19 bounded packets were configured for `gpt-6.2-sol` at ultra, and all 97 frozen input hashes matched. The selected lead settings were preserved; realized backend settings were unavailable. The exact chat source and native title were also unavailable, so the invocation and delivered updates were saved as an [unregistered partial public record](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors/chat-histories/PARTIAL_UNREGISTERED_DIR_20261124.md).
Please continue the research in accordance with the continuation note

I’ll read the continuation and current register, then take up the degree-zero first-eigenmap question. I’ll check which parts of the Hopf-lift argument use the topology of a homotopy sphere and which require an additional geometric estimate.

The Hopf lift gives a conditional obstruction. A great-\(S^2\) first eigenmap would force the first coexact one-form eigenvalue below \(\lambda_1/4\), and topology forces a rank-one point where Ricci curvature is nonpositive in one direction. Neither exclusion follows from the Yamabe hypothesis alone. I’m now testing what survives for maps whose image spans \(S^4\), including the energy cost of losing degree.

The degree calculation gives a sharp threshold. Losing one unit of degree costs at least \(16\operatorname{Vol}(S^4)\) in fourth-power energy, and a shrinking round bubble attains that cost. The estimate still requires a suitable metric and sequence. I’m now testing a construction available on every smooth homotopy four-sphere: prescribe a harmonic spinor at the Euclidean end of the punctured manifold and determine what would force it to be parallel.

The punctured construction works on every smooth homotopy four-sphere. A local metric deformation gives an invertible compact Dirac operator while preserving a flat ball. Its Green spinor then gives a unique harmonic field with a prescribed nonzero limit at infinity. The remaining issue is geometric: the field is parallel exactly when its weighted scalar-curvature integral vanishes. I’m checking whether conformal optimization or the Dirac equation itself supplies that control. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn656312269view6","turn656312269view7"]}}

The Green-spinor test exposed a limit: even with no interior zeros and fixed unit amplitude at infinity, its relative error can tend to zero while the self-dual Weyl energy diverges. A different argument now looks more promising for the original degree question. The fourth variation at a Yamabe minimizer appears to constrain the entire first eigenspace. I’m checking whether equality forces a full-span eigenmap to be a homothety.

The independent checks agree. On a unit-volume Yamabe minimizer with \(s=3\lambda_1\), the first scalar eigenspace has dimension at most five. If it has dimension five, its eigenfunctions give a homothetic diffeomorphism onto \(S^4\). This rules out a full-span degree-zero limit. I’m integrating the proof with the near-equality result, where the eigenfunction values can approach the round distribution even though smooth convergence is still unproved.

**The full-span degree-zero alternative is ruled out.** The continuation yielded a recognition theorem for any smooth, closed, connected four-manifold with a unit-volume Yamabe-minimizing metric \(g\). If \(s\) is its scalar curvature and \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_5\) are its first five positive scalar Laplace eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, then
\[
\frac35\sum_{i=1}^{5}\lambda_i-s\ge0,
\qquad
\text{with equality exactly when }(M,g)\text{ is round up to scale.}
\]

The decisive step is a fourth-variation estimate. At \(s=3\lambda_1\), every real first eigenfunction satisfies \(\int\phi^4\le(15/7)(\int\phi^2)^2\). Averaging over the eigenspace bounds its dimension by five. At dimension five, the normalized eigenfunctions give a homothetic diffeomorphism onto \(S^4\). Thus a degree-zero first eigenmap at this endpoint must lie in a proper great subsphere. The great-\(S^2\) and great-\(S^3\) cases remain open on a nonround homotopy sphere. [Proof and independent assessment](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors/reviews/DIR_B22_FIVE_EIGENFUNCTIONS_20261124.md)

There is also a near-equality result. Along positive-scalar Yamabe minimizers with \(3\lambda_5/s\to1\), the five normalized eigenfunctions have joint distribution converging to uniform measure on the unit \(S^4\). This controls what a volume-sampled point sees. A region of vanishing volume can still escape detection, so smooth recognition requires more. [Near-equality proof review](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors/notes/DIR_E47_20261124.md)

The punctured Dirac route supplied an unconditional construction: every smooth homotopy four-sphere admits a punctured metric with an exactly Euclidean end and a harmonic spinor of prescribed unit amplitude at infinity. An explicit family shows why parallelism remains a separate problem. Even genuine zero-free Green spinors can have relative error tending to zero while self-dual Weyl energy diverges. [Boundary construction and counterexample](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors/reviews/DIR_B19_GREEN_BOUNDARY_ASSESSMENT_20261124.md) genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn656312269view6","turn656312269view7"]}}

**The global gap is metric construction and smooth attainment.** The next decision, DIR-B23, tests whether attaching a shrinking punctured core to a round chamber preserves the five-eigenvalue condition *after Yamabe minimization*. A competing conformal test concentrated in the core is the first obstruction to check. [Continuation note](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors/continuation-notes/02_AFTER_FIVE_EIGENFUNCTION_RIGIDITY_20261124.md)
